title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] in SL(2,Z) has order 6. A_rho = Z[rho] is the ring of Eisenstein integers Z[zeta_6]. Given xi = [[A,B],[C,D]] in SL(2,Z) with Tr(xi rho) = Tr(rho), the conditions (16) are AD - BC = 1 and C + D - B = 1. One wants alpha with alpha rho alpha^{-1} rho^{-1} = xi, i.e. alpha rho alpha^{-1} = xi rho.

Over Z a solution alpha in GL(2,Z) exists. The reason is that xi rho makes Z^2 an invertible A_rho-module, and Pic(Z[zeta_6]) = 1.

This page: any solution has det alpha in Z^* = {±1} (18). Two solutions differ by right multiplication by the centralizer of rho, which is A_rho^* (the 6 units). Their determinant is the norm f f-bar > 0, hence equal to 1. So sign(det alpha) is an invariant of xi. If it is -1, the loop equation has no solution in SL(2,Z). Equivalently, xi rho is SL(2,Z)-conjugate to rho^{-1} rather than to rho; the order-6 elements with characteristic polynomial x^2 - x + 1 form two SL(2,Z)-classes, swapped by GL(2,Z).

Grothendieck notes that B and D already determine xi via (16). His other calculations suggest that the sign equals D mod 3 (+1 if D ≡ 1, -1 if D ≡ -1).

He then returns to a general base S = Spec A and rank-2 M. Given a solution alpha in Gamma GL(M), the other solutions are alpha f with f in A_rho^*. The next page derives that the obstruction to an SL-solution is the class of det alpha in A^*/N(A_rho^*). This is a class-field-theoretic norm-residue group. He asserts that for A = Z_l it vanishes except for l = 3, where it is Z/2.

Check/completion (my computation). Write M = xi rho. Then alpha = [v, -Mv] for any v, so det alpha = -q(v), where q(v) = det[v, Mv]. This q is a binary quadratic form of discriminant -3, hence definite. Evaluating at e1 gives -q(e1) = D, so sign(det alpha) = sign(D) exactly.

Eliminating C from (16) gives D(A+B) = B^2 + B + 1. This shows D ≠ 0 and sign D = sign(A+B), and that B, D determine A and C, confirming his remark. Since prime divisors of B^2 + B + 1 are 3 or ≡ 1 mod 3, and 9 never divides it, |D| ≡ 0 or 1 mod 3. So whenever 3 ∤ D, D ≡ sign(D) mod 3, and Grothendieck's conjecture is correct.

It fails to apply only when 3 | D. Example: xi = [[0,1],[-1,3]], where the sign is +1. Conceptually, D mod 3 is the 3-adic norm-residue invariant (Z_3^*/(1+3Z_3) = {±1}) and sign(D) is the archimedean invariant. The extension Q(zeta_3)/Q ramifies only at 3 and infinity, so reciprocity (product formula for the Hilbert symbol) forces the two to agree.
errors: The guess 'sign = D mod 3' is incomplete: D ≡ 0 mod 3 occurs (e.g. A=0, B=1, C=-1, D=3 satisfies (16)), and then the rule gives nothing. The correct global statement is sign(det alpha) = sign(D) (= sign(A+B)), which agrees with D mod 3 whenever 3 ∤ D.
The aside 'B, D determine xi' is right but needs the relation D(A+B) = B^2 + B + 1 (D is never 0); not an error, just unstated.

ideas.what: Determinant of a conjugating matrix modulo norms of the centralizer units as an obstruction to SL-conjugacy; sign invariant for order-6 elements in SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: GL vs SL conjugacy classes of torsion elements; obstruction in A^*/N(A_rho^*) (Latimer–MacDuffee / norm residue)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Latimer–MacDuffee, Taussky; conjugacy classes of torsion in SL(2,Z) are standard)

ideas.what: Identification of the global sign (real place) with D mod 3 (3-adic place) for solutions of the loop/commutator equation [alpha, rho] = xi
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert reciprocity for Q(sqrt(-3))/Q applied to binary forms of discriminant -3
ideas.where_published: Possibly related remarks in La Longue Marche (1981); unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures from computations that the SL-obstruction sign equals D mod 3. A complete elementary proof exists: sign = sign(D), and |D| ≡ 1 mod 3 when 3 ∤ D because D divides B^2+B+1. It is conceptually the agreement of the real and 3-adic norm-residue invariants. He leaves the conjecture unproved here, and it is incomplete when 3 | D.
missed.quote: les calculs faits par ailleurs suggèrent que ce signe est aussi égal au reste de D mod 3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it clarifies a small step in his 'équation des lacets' analysis of SL(2,Z) torsion relations. It is not new mathematics to a specialist.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine but nicely conceived link between an SL(2,Z) conjugacy obstruction and local class field theory, in exploratory notes on the loop equation. The conjectured formula is essentially right (sign = sign D, which matches D mod 3 when 3 ∤ D), but the content is classical.
transcription_corrections: 'f ∈ A_ζ^*' should be 'f ∈ A_ρ^*' (centralizer of ρ).
Reference to formulas should likely be '(16)', not '(15)'.
'(cas dans Sl(2,Z))' is probably '(*) dans Sl(2,Z)', i.e. no solution of equation (*) in SL(2,Z).
The symbol written ζ is the ξ of the previous page.
